title: Liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin
context_label: Platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
schedule_summary: Both medicines every four weeks, usually for six cycles. Extra cycles may be considered if the cancer shrinks or stays stable.
purpose: The aim is to control recurrent cancer and review how it responds.
indication_text: This combination uses the pegylated liposomal formulation of doxorubicin with carboplatin for cancer that has returned and is considered sensitive to platinum.
administration_text: Liposomal doxorubicin is given first, slowly at the start to watch for a reaction. Carboplatin follows. Report burning, swelling or pain around your drip immediately.
monitoring_summary: Your team considers symptoms and total anthracycline exposure.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.explanation: A fatty coating carries doxorubicin in the blood. The medicine damages DNA in dividing cells.
agents.mechanism: A fatty coating carries doxorubicin in the blood. The medicine damages DNA in dividing cells.
agents.watch: Report sore hands, feet or mouth before the next infusion, and report swelling or breathlessness promptly.

agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

common_effects.title: Nausea and vomiting · Chemotherapy
common_effects.text: Use your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Call if vomiting continues or you cannot drink.

common_effects.title: Hands and feet · Liposomal doxorubicin
common_effects.text: Report painful redness, peeling or blisters early. Tell the team if walking is affected.

common_effects.title: Mouth · Liposomal doxorubicin
common_effects.text: Report ulcers, pain on swallowing or difficulty drinking.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Infused medicines
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, wheeze or chest tightness during treatment.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Chemotherapy
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering, unexplained bleeding or suddenly feeling unwell? Call the oncology team now.

serious_effects.title: Kidneys · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if you pass much less urine or cannot keep fluids down. Kidney checks guide treatment.

questions.q: What changes to your hands, feet, mouth or breathing would you report before another infusion?
questions.a: Talk through this with your nurse and write the answer on your appointment sheet.

questions.a: Ask the team to fill in your wallet card with local numbers.

support.title: Skin and mouth care
support.text: Avoid rubbing or overheating sore hands and feet. Ask about moisturiser and mouth care. Report symptoms early, particularly when walking or eating becomes difficult.

support.title: Sickness prevention
support.text: Follow the written carboplatin anti-sickness plan. Contact the team if vomiting continues despite your prescribed rescue medicine.

consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.
urgent_extra: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.

evidence.title: CALYPSO
evidence.interpretation: In platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, median time to progression was 11.3 months with this combination versus 9.4 months with carboplatin and paclitaxel. The combinations had different side effects.
evidence.limitations: This comparison concerned recurrent disease. A median describes the trial group.
